description:
defstruct takes a default per field, but only a literal term. A default that computes or names something is refused with parse/struct-default (fixture 00860):

    defmodule Tally do
      defstruct [:name, count: Enum.count([1]), seen: MapSet.new()]
    end

Elixir has no struct-specific rule: a module body runs at definition (defstruct expands to quote bind_quoted), Kernel.Utils.defstruct escapes each value (:elixir_quote.escape; refs and closures refused), and %T{} uses the escaped value. That is the oracle.

Design (page fz-sc8.144.html v2, accepted): definition-time evaluation is a synthesized zero-arity macro whose body is Macro.escape(<expr>), expanded through the existing macro pipeline (World::macro_root, RootBackendProduct, run_macro_invocation) in the walk's namespace at that point; the walk waits on it as it does a macro call. The quoted code returned takes the expression's place, and StructForm parsing runs on it unchanged. A written literal is not run: the LiteralTerm::of test becomes the skip check, so every struct in lib/ today evaluates nothing (prediction: no pin moves). A call into the module being defined is refused in Elixir's words (fz-sc8.223). A PID is refused by Macro.escape (user decision); a remote capture is refused naming the gap until fz-sc8.226.

Goes away: LiteralTerm as a carrier (StructDef.defaults holds quoted source), the parse/struct-default refusal in parse_struct_field_default, fixture 00860.

Done when: oracle fixtures (call default, alias default, MapSet.new([1]), a default that prints once before main) match Elixir on interp/run/build; refusal fixtures for make_ref(), fn, local() and raise; a telemetry test shows a computed-default struct evaluates once however many literals read it and a literal-only struct evaluates nothing; distiller pins and census unchanged.
title: A defstruct default is any expression, evaluated in the defining module
